lesson.title: Nested Decisions
lesson.driving_question: How can a second decision run only when the first condition is met?
lesson.primary_concept_family: Dependent selection using a decision inside another decision
lesson.concept_budget: Place one complete if/else inside one outer branch; iteration is deferred.
misconceptions: The inner decision is reached only through its outer branch.
Each colon starts its own indented block.
An inner else belongs to the inner if at the same indentation level.
Different routes can ask different follow-up questions.
lesson.progression_note: Completes the Grade 6 selection strand by modelling dependent questions before loops begin.
code_expectations: a visible result on every route

primm.prompt: Recall how an if/else chooses one route and how indentation marks the lines belonging to a branch.
Use answers yes and then no. Trace the outer route and inner route before predicting the single displayed message.
Run all three routes: no; yes then no; yes then yes. Record the message produced by each route.

questions: Why is the windy question skipped when the first answer is no?
If you answer yes to raining and no to windy, what message appears?
Which if does the inner else belong to, and how does indentation show this?
What route is taken for an unexpected first answer such as maybe, and why?

primm.prompt: Change the inner decision to ask for wind strength: strong or light. When raining is "yes", strong wind must display "Wear a coat." and light wind must display "Take an umbrella." Keep the dry-weather route unchanged. Test two runs: raining yes with strong wind, then raining yes with light wind.

Change the decision for when [raining] is "no". Ask whether it is sunny and store the answer in [sunny]. Display "Take sunglasses." when [sunny] is "yes"; otherwise display "No weather gear needed." Keep the two rain outputs unchanged. Test "no" and "yes"; display "Take sunglasses." Test "no" and "no"; display "No weather gear needed."

Ask whether the visitor has a library card and store the answer in [has_card]. Use a nested if statement. When [has_card] is "yes", ask whether a book is overdue and store the answer in [overdue]. Display "Return the overdue book first." when [overdue] is "yes"; otherwise display "You may borrow a book." When [has_card] is "no", display "Apply for a library card." Test "yes" and "yes", "yes" and "no", then "no"; verify all three outputs.
Repair the indentation and the missing colon so each inner route belongs to the windy decision.

blocks.definition: A decision placed inside one route of another decision.
The first test that controls whether an inner decision can be reached.
A second test made only inside the selected outer route.
A question that is relevant only after an earlier answer.
The horizontal position that shows which block owns a line.
